input.notes: National Park Service. Base year April 1, 2027 – March 31, 2028 plus four option years (to March 31, 2032); FAR 52.217-8 extension up to 6 months possible. Three cleaning seasons (PWS 1.5): Peak = Friday before Memorial Day through Labor Day (May 28 – Sept 6, 2027, 102 days); Shoulder = May 1 to start of Peak and day after Labor Day through Oct 15; Winter = Oct 16 – Apr 30. Mowing season May 1 – Oct 15 (approx. 24 weeks); price 24 cycles Type I, 8 cycles Type II, 1 cycle Type III (A6). Snow and ice removal by NPS, not part of contract (PWS 3.2). Each seasonal facility gets one opening and one closing clean (PWS 2.4). Table 3-C campsite and site policing (counts, not areas): Birch Point Loops A/B/C 34/32/30 sites and fire rings (7X/WK Peak, 3X/WK Shoulder); Pine Island 6 boat-in sites, 6 fire rings (1X/WK with VT-58); picnic areas 18 grills (with shelter service); 46 bear-resistant trash/recycling containers. Wage Determination 2015-5013 Rev 27 (Janitor 11150; Laborer, Grounds Maintenance 11030).

input.summary: Tamarack Lakes NRA (NPS) janitorial and grounds PWS 140P6127Q0018 with Amendment 0001. TE-1: 34 rows registered (29 serviced, 46,274 SF as printed; 121 excluded N/S, 312 and 412 excluded CONC, 413 demolished, 214 option-only CLIN 0004). Amendment 0001: Bldg. 101 revised to 12,940 SF and 10/3/10 fixtures, VT-56 deleted, PS-22 Shoulder 2X/WK, VT-60 Lost Creek vault toilet (144 SF) added -> 29 serviced, 47,426 SF. Bldg. 120 cleanable 1,240 SF of 8,960 SF gross. Grounds: Table 3-A 67.1 ac (27.3 Type I, 25.8 Type II, 14.0 Type III; G-1 split across Bldgs. 101/102/104), Table 3-B 223,500 SF parking + W-1 9,850 SF walks + W-2 trail 76,032 SF (9,504 LF x 8 ft), plus Amendment P-6 12,400 SF aggregate lot. Incumbent North Country Facility Services, LLC, 140P6122C0009, $2,731,460 / 60 months, OY4 $574,920 (janitorial only).
unresolved: TE-1 frequencies vary by season (Peak / Shoulder / Winter); service_level carries the Peak-season frequency and service_season the open–close window, with Shoulder and Winter frequencies in service_frequency_text and notes only — shoulder/winter visits are lower than the Peak rate (e.g. VT-41 7X/WK Peak, 2X/WK Shoulder, 1X/WK Winter; VT-51/VT-52 3X/WK Peak, 1X/WK rest of year; Bldg. 101 Winter 5X/WK).

Bldg. 310 Sandy Bay Beach House is 2X/DAY (twice daily, 7 days) for the Peak season and Bldg. 101 main-level public restrooms are 2X/DAY in Peak; no service level expresses two services per day (recorded as daily_7 with notes).

Table 3-C Campsite and Site Policing (102 campsites incl. 6 Pine Island sites, 102 fire rings, 18 grills, 46 bear-resistant containers) is counts only, with no grounds kind to register; recorded in site notes.
W-2 Lakeshore Paved Trail printed as 9,504 LF, 8 ft wide; registered as 76,032 sqft (length x width).

Narrative-only items out of scope: composting toilets at the 14 backcountry campsites and 3 portable toilets at the North Arm ice-fishing access (PWS 2.5(e)); portable toilet at Loon Narrows replacing VT-56 (separate contract); vault/septic pumping (PWS 2.5(f)); natural-surface trails, beach grooming and snow removal (PWS 3.2, 3.4).
TE-1 printed total 46,274 SF is the as-issued serviced total; Amendment 0001 Change 6 revises it to 47,426 SF (Area A 30,668 SF, Area E 1,740 SF).
